Modified response incorporating Beige Book context:

- Policy stance: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50 percent and continued QT at the existing caps ($60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS). O/N repo set at 5.5% and O/N RRP at 5.3%. Statement remains data dependent and “highly attentive to inflation risks.”
- Beige Book overlay: The latest District reports point to largely flat-to-slight growth overall. Consumer spending is mixed—goods softer while leisure/travel remains solid in several Districts. Manufacturing is flat to down; freight and inventories reflect softer final demand. Residential real estate remains subdued amid high mortgage rates; multifamily supply is tempering rent growth. CRE conditions have deteriorated further, especially in office; New York District real estate contacts remain pessimistic with rising vacancies and concessions. Labor markets are easing—hiring has become less difficult, job openings have edged down, and wage growth is moderating (still above pre-pandemic). Price pressures continue to moderate across many categories, though services inflation remains sticky. Credit conditions have tightened and loan demand has softened; some Districts note a gradual uptick in delinquencies from low levels.
- Implications: Beige Book evidence of slower momentum, easing labor demand, moderating price pressures, and tighter credit reinforces the FOMC’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and policy lags. This reduces the near-term need for additional firming unless inflation re-accelerates or disinflation stalls.
- Net read: Relative to the statement’s vigilant tone, Beige Book signals incremental downside risks to growth and continued disinflationary progress, shifting the balance from mildly hawkish to more balanced/slightly cautious.
